about: Upgrade paths and rollback, one entry per release, oldest first (#221, #222). min_from_version: the oldest release that upgrades directly to this one, applying the steps of every release after it, in order. rollback_without_restore: whether the previous release boots and serves on the control-plane schema and the catalogs this release leaves; when false, rollback_blocked_by says why, and only a restore of the backup taken before the upgrade goes back. The manager reads this file at boot (ReleaseGate) and release_manifest.py copies the release's entry into release.json. changesets: the Liquibase changelog files the release adds. release.sh adds the next release's entry when it moves version.sbt to its snapshot; a pull request adding a changelog file lists it there, and one adding a one-way change (a drop, a rename, a type change, a new NOT NULL, a DuckDB or DuckLake bump that migrates catalogs) sets rollback_without_restore false and says why. release_manifest.py --check-pins refuses a changelog file no entry lists, and a one-way one under rollback_without_restore true.

rollback_blocked_by: Liquibase 0055 drops qodstate_pool.lockdown, which 0.10.x reads: a 0.10.x manager fails at boot with column "lockdown" does not exist

steps.text: Back up the control-plane database: Liquibase 0047 to 0055 run at boot and 0055 is one way.
Replace the static API key with personal access tokens and remove QOD_API_KEY everywhere: a manager ignores it and warns.

Unset QOD_ACL_FILTERED_METADATA and QOD_ACL_DIALECT (refused at any value), and QOD_ACL_ENABLED and QOD_NODE_LOCKDOWN (refused when off), with their quack-flightsql.acl.* and quack-flightsql.nodeLockdown keys.
Grant tenant users what they read: enforcement can no longer be turned off and per-pool lockdown is gone. On OPA tenants, update the policies for the node's input (columns, via, locations).
If users load files, set QOD_TENANT_FILES_ROOT, and list in QOD_USER_S3_ALLOWED_ENDPOINTS any endpoint other than AWS their own S3 keys target.

In fleet mode set QOD_INTERNAL_URL on every manager; on Kubernetes without the chart set QOD_POD_IP. The REST port + 1 must be free, or set QOD_INTERNAL_PORT. Under HA, set QOD_NODE_KEY_SECRET to one value on every replica, or on none.

With the Helm chart, unset env.QOD_INTERNAL_URL, env.QOD_INTERNAL_PORT and env.QOD_POD_IP (helm upgrade fails on them), and size the pod for a 2 GiB heap and 512 MiB of direct memory, or set javaOpts.
Upgrade every HA replica together (scale to one replica or use a Recreate rollout), and upgrade the qod CLI with the manager, on every fleet server too.

Restart every node (node protocol 6); on Kubernetes pull this release's node image. Read the boot log's WARN and ERROR lines about untrusted initSql, sql federation sources and parked clientSecretRef values.
Back up the control-plane database: Liquibase 0056 runs at boot and adds the three-way merge columns to qodstate_branch_merge.
On Kubernetes, read your maintenance policies: a database with maintenance enabled runs it for the first time after this upgrade.
On OPA tenants, a rule keyed on columns no longer refuses a branch's change count, which is asked with columns: []: refuse on the table instead.
Under HA, finish a rolling upgrade before merging a branch.
Propose again any branch proposal made before the upgrade: its merge is refused 409 proposal_stale.
Back up the control-plane database: Liquibase 0057 runs at boot and adds a policy-version trigger on object-store keys.

Give every database whose metastore names another Postgres server its own pgUser and pgPassword (qod database update): QoD's login is no longer filled in there, and such a database stops connecting at its next node start.
Recompile any manager module calling PoolSupervisor.createTenantDb: it now states writerTrusted.
Upgrade the node image and fleet servers with the manager, and restart every node.
Run the manager on Java 25 or later (qod start and qod serve download a Temurin 25 JRE when none is found; run-jar.sh and run-jar.ps1 need JAVA_HOME or java on PATH at 25).
A manager launched with -cp passes --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED and --sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access=allow itself.
Correct any database's defaultSchema or defaultDatabase that is not a plain identifier before its next update or manifest import.
Replace any personal access token that administers QoD under verbCeiling RO: it is now read-only on admin REST and MCP too.
Set QOD_MAINT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MIN above the longest full maintenance chain of your largest database: it now caps the whole chain, and its default rises from 60 to 240 minutes.
Clear any database's defaultDatabase that names another catalog than its own (qod database update --default-database ''): it is ignored, and create and update refuse it.
Under HA, an upgraded leader can fail as stale a maintenance run still executing on a replica of the earlier release; the next tick queues it again.
Upgrade the node image and fleet servers with the manager, and restart every node: until a node restarts, each real authorization outage on it reads as a denial instead of a retryable UNAVAILABLE.
